statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-92262 is MariaDB advisory GHSA-65jj-h265-3m7h (MDEV-40362): https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-65jj-h265-3m7h . The #mysql50# prefix let a table or database name bypass the normal table-name filesystem encoding, so a user could reach files under their legacy unencoded names and cause crashes, data corruption, data exfiltration or code execution. MariaDB fixed it in 11.8.9 (and 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 12.3.3 and 13.0.2) with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/f277eefa424850a8cba5c2371406047f6395e8bb and the test follow-up https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/574ba66b2d6c5d71db83d416677876e9b592858e : the server rejects new #mysql50#-prefixed names outside ALTER DATABASE ... UPGRADE DATA DIRECTORY NAME through a new error_if_mysql50_prefix() check, and Lex_ident_fs::check_body in sql/table.cc accepts the prefix only for names that do not decode as normal encoded filenames. Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 does not include it; Debian fixes trixie in 1:11.8.9+ds-0+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-92262). DHI backports the commit's server changes, adapted only to the 11.8.6 forms of the functions they touch, and the fixed version is the third build, the first that carries them. We compared all four published builds of Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 in the DHI Debian repository (called the first to fourth build below; the fourth is the current build) on amd64 and arm64; each package we read was verified against the repository index checksum, reading the dynamic symbol tables of /usr/sbin/mariadbd (mariadb-server-core) and of the embedded server library libmariadbd.so.19 (libmariadbd19t64). error_if_mysql50_prefix is absent in the first and second builds and present in the third and fourth (62 bytes on amd64, 80 on arm64), and Lex_ident_fs::check_body grows from 266 to 440 bytes on amd64 and from 328 to 612 on arm64 between the second and third builds, the same in both files. From the third build on, mariadb-test-data carries the upstream MDEV-40362 regression tests, which the first two builds lack, and the shipped changelog lists this CVE.
